lines.text: What if every wheel on Earth turned *square*... for five seconds?
Times Square. Three hundred and fifty-two cars, rolling along at about *eighteen* kilometers an hour.
Square wheels in three... two... one.
Every quarter turn lifts the car... and *slams* it back down.
Each corner raises the axle almost *fourteen centimeters*. At this speed, that's seven slams every second.
But here's the weird part. A square wheel *can* roll perfectly smoothly, on a road made of upside-down *catenary* curves.
Follow for more. What should change next?
